plan: dispatch://INFRA-257/artifact/plan-md (version 1) is the full plan: files read, measurements, design decisions, ordered tasks, the exact Job manifest and script for the proof, tester and reviewer checks, the production check.
summary: Add gcc and libc6-dev to the runtime stage's single apt line in packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile (no new layer). Keep cgo off by default two ways: CGO_ENABLED=0 added to the existing final-stage ENV instruction (with imageEnv in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/operatorpod.go), and CGO_ENABLED=0 appended to /opt/go/go.env in the toolchain stage. Add gcc to the capability toolchain row (image.go, capabilities.go Summary, capabilitiestest stubs, image_test.go detail), gcc --version to the toolchain smoke step, gcc and libc6-dev to the licence intro string (unless INFRA-255 landed first), docs/kubernetes.md and running-legion.md, and supersede the stale race/cgo learnings. Prove both acceptance lines with a Kubernetes Job running the PR head's worker image by digest (worker security context, gVisor) and the same Job on a before image as the negative control; record sizes in the PR.

proofSurface.acceptance1: Job on the head image: CGO_ENABLED=1 go -C packages/envoy test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./internal/bus/ prints ok and exits 0 with no CC, CXX or linker override; a racy canary built with CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -race and run as a binary prints WARNING: DATA RACE and exits 66. Negative control: the same Job on the before image fails with cgo: C compiler "gcc" not found.
proofSurface.acceptance2: Same Job: go env CGO_ENABLED is 0; a default go build records CGO_ENABLED=0 (go version -m); env -i keeps 0 (go.env); GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 keeps 0 (ENV); the supervise table test passes with no override. Controls: CGO_ENABLED=1 build records 1; a copy of /opt/go without the go.env line under env -i prints 1. Production check in the implementer's pod repeats them, including from the real Python eval kernel.

implement: legion-worker: push procedure, PR body template, E2E proof rules and the simplify pass (references/pr-body.md); conflicts-and-rewrites.md if INFRA-255 merges first and the PR conflicts
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the diff that references/pr-body.md requires before completion
envoy: subscribe to the PR's checks topic to wait for the Worker Image build without polling
dispatch: any Dispatch write (a finding ask or a note on the issue)
test: legion-worker: verifying the implementer's proof and writing the tester's own proof array (references/pr-body.md)
envoy: wait for the Worker Image run on the PR's checks topic without polling
review: legion-worker: review threads, approval of the head and the merge gate (references/review-threads.md, references/merge-gate.md)

findings.finding: 'Default Go builds use CGO_ENABLED=0' can mean the go command only or every Go build consumer; /opt/go/go.env covers cmd/go but not go/build-library readers (go/build reads only the process environment and defaults cgo on), and go test passes the original environment to test binaries.
findings.answer: The plan adds ENV CGO_ENABLED=0 beside the go.env line, so inheriting go/build readers (the supervise table tests, measured failing today with go tool cgo: exit status 2 and passing with CGO_ENABLED=0) get 0; the proof runs that test with no override. The remaining boundary (a scrubbed environment and a go/build reader) is stated in decision 2 and gets Go's own default, which works with gcc present.

findings.finding: A toolchain switch (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, a go.mod toolchain line) execs another GOROOT whose go.env lacks the line, so go.env alone does not cover it.
findings.answer: The ENV passes through the switch (the toolchain is exec'd with the process environment); the proof's switched-toolchain check runs GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go env CGO_ENABLED and expects 0. Automatic switching is not disabled.

findings.finding: A build Job running the candidate image differs from a Sandbox worker pod (volumes, operator ServiceAccount, Oh My Pi process, Python eval kernel); the plan must state the Job's fidelity contract and what it does not reproduce.
findings.answer: The Job uses the worker container's security context (uid/gid/fsGroup 1000, no escalation, capabilities dropped, RuntimeDefault seccomp), gVisor, the image's own ENV and PATH, scratch on an emptyDir, an explicit bash command, and records the pod's imageID; env -i stands in for the eval kernel and is named a stand-in. The production check exercises the real pod, bash tool and Python eval kernel.

findings.finding: The before image for the size record is not named; no image exists for the base commit, and the apt change also rebuilds the natives layer, so the total delta is not gcc's alone.
findings.answer: Task 9 first dispatches a like-for-like base build on main (sha-81a3b5ef7b47), else uses the newest ancestor image as a disclosed fallback naming its revision and the input diff. The size block records layer counts, byte sums, revisions, the total delta, the apt layer's delta and which other layers changed; the 57,158,352-byte .deb figure is an estimate only.
